::: {#exm-relation-power}
#### Powers of "beats"

For the relation $B$ of @exm-beats,
$B^2 = B \circ B$ (@def-relation-power) relates $a$ to $c$ when $a$ beats something that beats $c$:

$$
B^2 = \set{(\text{rock}, \text{paper}), (\text{scissors}, \text{rock}), (\text{paper}, \text{scissors})},
$$

which is the inverse $B^{-1}$ of @exm-inverse-relation.
Then $B^3 = B^2 \circ B$ relates each element to itself:

$$
B^3 = \set{(\text{rock}, \text{rock}), (\text{paper}, \text{paper}), (\text{scissors}, \text{scissors})},
$$

as following three arrows of @fig-beats leads back to the start.
So $B^4 = B^3 \circ B = B$, and the powers of $B$ repeat after every three steps.

For the relation $P$ of @exm-parent,
$P^2$ is the grandparent relation of @exm-relation-composition,
and $P^3 = \emptyset$, since no one in $F$ has a great-grandchild in $F$.

:::
